issues.description: The problem statement requires that constructors take attributes in the same order as in the UML diagram (first attribute on top => first parameter). In the UML ExcellenceLand shows attributes 'excellencyLevel' then 'excellentEnough' (and the tasks additionally require a private List<Ride> rides). However, the solution implements ExcellenceLand's constructor with parameters in the order (List<Ride> rides, boolean excellentEnough, double excellencyLevel), which conflicts with the UML-based ordering required by the problem statement. This mismatch will confuse students about the expected constructor parameter order and may cause tests or grading to fail if they implement the constructor following the UML/instructions.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the constructor parameter order with the UML/instruction. Either (A) change ExcellenceLand's constructor in the solution (and any tests) to accept parameters in UML order, e.g. (double excellencyLevel, boolean excellentEnough, List<Ride> rides) and assign them accordingly, or (B) update the problem statement/UML to explicitly list 'rides' as the first attribute if that ordering is intended. Ensure the template, solution, and tests consistently use the same parameter order.
